text:
oncall-runbook-bot: P1 alert: sustained p99 TLS handshake spikes + streaming tail stalls in eu-west-2 starting ~09:03 UTC. Auto-page sent to #incidents and oncall list. Please acknowledge and follow incident runbook.
Carlos Diaz: ack. grabbing context: p95 ~230ms, p99 currently ~2.4s on inference egress. Streaming chunk timeouts observed by 4 customers. I'll be lead for now.
Mei Lin: I'm on call rotation, can take handoff in 10m. quick ask: which egress path? is this NAT or loadbalancer?
SRE: initial telemetry shows NAT instance cpu & conntrack churn on nat-eu-west-2a; ephemeral port exhaustion patterns at ~09:01 UTC. Kernel dropped connections and retransmit rate spiked.
netops: we also have a correlating bump in inter-AZ latency and queue drops on switch-azb-azc paths; cloud provider reports increased HC swaps in that zone (ticket CP-9001 opened).
support: customers reporting stalled streaming and reconnect loops. No full API 5xxs but higher latency and client-side aborts. sharing templated update.
Carlos Diaz: mitigation plan: (A) steer new egress to same-AZ egress (mesh policy) as immediate mitigation; (B) increase NAT fleet capacity + widen ephemeral port range; (C) enable TLS session resumption and reduce cert chain size for short-term.
Mei Lin: runbook command to patch mesh: 
```
redwoodctl mesh update traffic-policy --service=inference-gw --egress=prefer-local --percent=30
```
SRE: applying canary 30% now. Also bumping conntrack and ephemeral port range:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 65535"
```
deploy-bot: mesh canary 30% applied id: mesh-20260315-09. NAT autoscale started +3 instances id: nat-asg-327. Monitor window 3m.
obs-bot: baseline before fixes: p99 handshake 2.41s, streaming success 88.7%. after 3m canary: canary p99 890ms, global p99 1.6s.
netops: tcpdump shows SYN->SYN retransmits, out-of-order seq, and occasional ICMP fragmentation-needed on path, which could point to MTU clamping/asymmetric route. also dns cache misses for internal nat hostnames around spike.
Carlos Diaz: good catch. for safety enable client keepalive to avoid repeated handshakes; push a quick config to gateway:
```
# gateway keepalive tweak
gateway.conf: keepalive_timeout=30s
```
Mei Lin: provider spun up replacement switch hardware in affected POD per CP-9001 update. they expect stabilization in 10-20m.
SRE: after nat scale and conntrack change, ephemeral port exhaustion stopped; conntrack churn down 70%. packet loss on cross-AZ path reduced from 1.3% -> 0.2%.
support: sending status to impacted customers: "We observed increased handshake latency and streaming stalls in eu-west-2, mitigations in progress; next update in 15m." 
Carlos Diaz: target to reach p99 < 600ms before we consider resolved. continue ramp canary to 60% then 100% if stable.
obs-bot: 12m after mitigation: p95 160ms, p99 520ms, streaming success 99.0%.
netops: collecting full tcptrace and conntrack dumps for postmortem. saving capture id tcpdump-eu2-20260315.
Mei Lin: taking over incident from Carlos. Carlos, please document timeline and handoff notes in postmortem doc and assign owner for follow-up actions.
Carlos Diaz: will owner postmortem: Carlos Diaz + netops. follow-ups: permanent conntrack tuning, review NAT autoscale thresholds, add MTU/path-check in our e2e tests, and add TLS session-resumption test in CI.
oncall-runbook-bot: Incident moved to Recovery. Create postmortem, attach captures, timeline, and provider ticket CP-9001. Keep monitoring for 1 hour.
Mei Lin: demoting to P2, leaving watch rotations. great job team. :white_check_mark:
